messages:
alex: Heads up — deploybot failed when promoting build 20260317-rc3 to prod. It looks like the manifest for tag `service-api:20260317-rc3` is sparse/missing a platform layer.

alex: Log snippet:```
deploybot: promote -> prod
registry: 400 Bad Request: manifest invalid: missing layer for platform linux/arm64
deploybot: aborting promotion, leaving tag pinned but not promoted
```

deploy-bot: Automatic message: Promotion aborted at 2026-03-17T14:00:10Z. Reason: manifest validation error from ECR backend. No rollback performed automatically.

maya: Is this a provenance/attestation reject or a manifest assembly issue? Any attestation errors in the payload?

alex: No attestation error logged. The artifact was built by the CI job, uploaded, cosign signed, and attestation attached. The registry is returning a missing layer at the manifest level (arm64). Only amd64 layers present per `skopeo inspect`.

julian: Sounds like the multi-arch manifest list didn't include the arm64 manifest. Could be a push race where the arm64 blob failed to upload but the manifest list was created. We should avoid reusing the same tag until we decide. Options: 1) pin callers to previous digest and rollback, 2) republish a complete multi-arch image under a new tag and do a canary promote, 3) attempt to push missing manifest blob into the same digest (risky).

paige: We have a tight change window until 16:00 PT. Canary already on 2 hosts in eu-west; traffic is low but not zero. I'd prefer rollback to the last good digest to minimize user impact. We can republish a corrected build under `20260317-rc3-fix1` afterwards and do a controlled promote tomorrow.

alex: Agreed. We should also prevent deploybot from retrying the same tag automatically. Can we set a temporary block?

deploy-bot: Note: deploybot attempted 2 retries and then aborted. Current behavior: will not retry tag promote without new tag or manual override. You can run `/deploybot promote --force TAG` but immutability policy may reject force retag.

julian: immutability is enabled in ECR for prod repos, so retagging an existing tag to point to a different digest is not allowed. To put the corrected image under the same human-friendly tag we'd need a new tag and then update release notes and redirect traffic. For immediate rollback use the previous digest: `service-api@sha256:8f7a...`

julian: Quick commands to check and rollback:```
# confirm previous digest
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name prod/service-api --image-ids imageTag=stable --query 'images[0].imageId.imageDigest'
# trigger rollback via deploybot (will deploy stable digest)
/deploybot rollback service-api --to-digest sha256:8f7a... --reason "manifest missing arm64 in rc3"
```

sre-oncall: I'm standing by to open the emergency change window. Recommend: 30m window, no other deploys, DO NOT attempt retagging the broken `20260317-rc3` tag. We'll coordinate network and registry console access in case we need to inspect blobs.

paige: I'll update the release notes and the release channel with a rollback notice and ETA. Also will create the follow-up ticket for republishing with a fix and a smaller canary slice for tomorrow.

alex: OK executing rollback now. I'll run the `/deploybot rollback` and ping when prod is back to stable. Thanks everyone.

paige: Thanks — post the rollback completion and the prod pod restart counts. I'll include it in the changelog entry. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Change window opened at 2026-03-17T14:05:00Z. No other deploys approved. Monitoring on standby.
